name: Wright Park
title: Ancient Trees in Wright Park, Tacoma: 8 to Find
meta_description: A red oak planted for Theodore Roosevelt in 1903, a 1939 sequoia, and a European and an American chestnut side by side in Tacoma's labelled park.
intro: Tacoma planted a red oak in Wright Park when Theodore Roosevelt came to town in May 1903, and the sign on its trunk still carries the year. Signs are how this park works. More than 400 of its trees wear a Metro Parks label, so the bark tells you which trunk you have found. The park was donated to the city in 1886 and has filled since with trees from other places. A giant sequoia went in for the 150th anniversary of the Constitution in 1939 and is now about 6.6 metres round. A tulip tree and a rock elm, a species seldom met in the Pacific Northwest, were planted somewhere between the late 1800s and the early 1900s. The best stop is a pair of chestnuts 25 metres apart, one European and one American, the second from a species that blight nearly wiped out. Entry is free, and October brings the red oak's colour, the tulip tree's yellow and the chestnuts dropping from their burs.
